title: Introductions and endings
summary: Open directly, establish a clear direction and finish by resolving the response with significance or consequence rather than repeating the introduction mechanically.

sections.title: The middle earns the ending
content: E7.1–E7.3 built purposeful, developed and connected body paragraphs. The introduction should now make the response easy to enter, while the ending should show what those paragraphs have established. Neither section can rescue an unfocused middle with grand language.

For the task ‘Write about something learned at school that you used or could use in different areas of your life’, the working response is specific: breaking a large task into clear next actions helped organise a charity sale and adapt safely when rain disrupted it. The opening points towards that route; the ending resolves why it matters.

sections.title: Open with orientation and direction
content: A direct introduction usually performs two jobs. It orients the reader to the situation or central idea, then establishes the direction of the response. ‘School projects taught me that a large problem becomes manageable when it is divided into clear next actions. I later relied on that method while organising a charity sale, especially when sudden rain forced our team to change plans.’

The first sentence answers the task without copying it. The second identifies the experience and creates a route through the essay. It does not waste time defining ‘learning’, asking a rhetorical question, announcing ‘In this essay I will’, or making an unsupported claim about every student.

sections.title: Promise only what the response will deliver
content: An introduction is a promise about scope and direction. If the body explains planning and adaptation, the opening should not promise a survey of teamwork, confidence, technology and leadership as well. A narrow, fulfilled direction is stronger than an impressive list the essay cannot develop.

Choose the amount of background that the reader needs now. One sentence can identify the lesson and one can locate the later experience. Save the drinks order, extension lead and sequence of decisions for the body, where those specifics can be explained rather than rushed.

sections.title: Resolve instead of replay
content: A useful ending returns to the controlling focus after the evidence has changed or deepened it. ‘The sale showed me that planning is not the same as predicting every problem. Its real value is giving people a clear next action when circumstances change.’ This resolves the response by turning the experience into a precise insight.

A mechanical ending merely replays earlier wording: ‘In conclusion, breaking tasks into steps helped the sale and the rain problem.’ A weak ending may also introduce an unproved new achievement, attach a generic moral such as ‘Therefore everyone should work hard’, or continue the story after its central problem has already been resolved.

sections.title: Make the two ends answer each other
content: Test the opening and ending as a pair. Circle the direction established at the start, then underline the insight or consequence reached at the end. The ending should answer the opening at a deeper level: clear steps initially made a large task manageable; after the rain, the writer understood that the same structure also made adaptation calmer and safer.

Do not force a repeated hook. A question in the first line does not need a slogan in the last. What matters is conceptual closure: the response has travelled from an initial claim through evidence to a more exact understanding.

sections.title: Diagnose the weak boundary
content: Classify introduction problems as delayed entry, copied task wording, empty generalisation, mechanical announcement, excessive detail or an overpromised roadmap. Classify ending problems as repetition, new evidence, an unrelated moral, exaggerated significance or an unresolved central focus.

Repair the exact problem. Cut throat-clearing before adding a stronger first sentence. Narrow a roadmap before polishing it. In an ending, state what the evidence now shows; do not add a fresh episode that would require another body paragraph.

sections.title: Enter directly and leave with resolution
content: Make six decisions about orientation, direction, scope, closure, new evidence and matched openings and endings. Complete the group before viewing feedback.
